Hannah - Customer Success: Quick ask after the Q&A: drop one short line per deal on why we won/lost so we can prioritize follow-ups. Keeping it brief please.
Ravi - Product: Win — Lumina picked us for predictable token costs + our streaming API; they specifically liked the console trace timeline.
Ari - Sales: Loss — FableBank required HSM + SOC2 Type II evidence; our Dedicated offering was fine functionally but procurement paused for certs.
Kai - Eng: Tech note on FableBank: long transcripts + strict audit windows caused tail latency and log retention questions. We have a prototype HSM adapter but need security signoff.
Lena - Marketing: Lumina case looks great for a short social post (pending permission). I'll draft a blurb.
Jon - CEO: Pattern: startups buy developer velocity, banks buy compliance. Priorities: 1) Sales battlecard on compliance gaps; 2) Dedicated onboarding checklist; 3) short eng runbook for long-sequence workloads. Ravi, can Product take 1+2?
Ravi - Product: Yep — I'll own the battlecard and checklist. Need Eng + Sales SMEs to review. Ari, who from AE can help?
Ari - Sales: I'll loop in Priya + Nate for reviews. Also request a 1-page risk note to attach to RFPs.
Hannah - Customer Success: I'll post the impacted deals list and exact asks by EOD.
Kai - Eng: I'll draft the long-seq runbook (runbook.md stub + prefix-cache snippet) and aim for EOW.
Lena - Marketing: Also suggest a 1-pager "why teams pick Redwood" for dev-focused GTM (bullets: unified runtime, cost predictability, rollout safety).
Jon - CEO: Good. Leah on Product + Ari + Hannah sync and deliver drafts next Tue. task-bot: created task RW-1999 "all-hands: compliance battlecard & long-seq runbook" and assigned to Ravi + Kai.
Hannah - Customer Success: Posted deals: Lumina (won), FableBank (lost), NovaOps (won on cost), SecureCo (lost on encryption). Link: <https://docs.redwood.ai/internal/all-hands/hotlist-1867000123>
Jon - CEO: Thanks team — keep updates short in this thread so we can track. :rocket:
